title: General Scholium
author: Isaac Newton
full_title: Philosophiæ naturalis principia mathematica. Editio secunda auctior et emendatior
source: The *Scholium generale* that closes Book III of Newton's *Philosophiæ naturalis principia mathematica*, 2nd ed. (Cambridge, 1713), where it was first printed.
transcribed_from: the [page images](https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_SyNF4RBbkIgC/page/n514/mode/2up) of a copy digitised by Google Books, on the Internet Archive.
copyright: In the public domain. Newton died in 1727; the scan carries the Public Domain Mark.
summary: Newton's closing statement to the Principia. He rejects Descartes's vortices, argues that the ordered system of Sun, planets and comets could only come from an intelligent and powerful Being, describes God by his dominion, and admits that he has not found the cause of gravity's properties: 'Hypotheses non fingo.' He ends by hinting at a subtle spirit behind cohesion, electricity, light and sensation.
